result.rationale: The diff shows `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod safeParse result object (e.g., `refreshTokenResponse` with `.success`/`.data`), and in GoogleCalendarService the code does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` then persists `data: { key }` directly. Unlike other call sites (e.g., office365, zoom) which use `.data` from the returned envelope, Google persists the whole envelope as credential.key, corrupting the stored credential after the first refresh. Verifiable from the diff.

judged_text: GoogleCalendarService persists the Zod safeParse envelope ({success, data}) returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse directly as credential.key instead of the parsed credential data. The first Google token refresh after this deploy overwrites the stored credential with {success: true, data: {...}}; the next GoogleCalendarService instantiation fails googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) (no access_token/refresh_token at the top level), so every Google Calendar operation - booking creation, updates, availability - throws for that user until they manually re-authorize the app.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the helper returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (an envelope with `{ success, data }`), not the parsed token payload itself (`return refreshTokenResponse;`). In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed credential is persisted as `key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` and then stored directly via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That will write `{success: true, data: {...}}` into `credential.key`, changing the stored shape and breaking later code that expects the token fields at the top level (previously it used `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which returns the payload).
